queue.title: Agent creation posts to the selected project, not the one you clicked
queue.severity: high — silently creates agents in the wrong project
queue.confirmed: Yes, traced end to end tonight. Not a hypothesis.
queue.evidence: hub/ui/src/App.tsx:474 sets agentCreateProjectId from the rail's per-project add button. App.tsx:516-524 renders <AgentCreateDialog open onClose onCreated /> and NEVER passes it — the value is used only to gate the render and to pick the post-create navigation target at line 522. Inside the dialog, useCreateAgent (hub/ui/src/api/agents.ts:318-329) posts to `/api/v1/projects/${selectedProjectId}/agents`. useCharters() and useProviderLaunchability(), also used by the dialog (AgentCreateDialog.tsx:150-152), read selectedProjectId too — so the charter list offered belongs to the wrong project as well.
queue.repro: With project A selected in the rail, expand project B and click its add-agent button. The agent is created in A; you are then navigated to B's page for an agent that is not there. If A already has an agent of that name you get 409 'already exists in this project' — true, but about the wrong project. This is exactly what the operator hit with a 'Spec' agent.
queue.operator_decision: Create in the clicked project AND switch selection to it. Chosen over 'leave selection alone' because every hook in that dialog reads selectedProjectId, and threading an explicit id through all of them is precisely the kind of thing that silently regresses — which is how this bug happened.
queue.do: Make the rail's add-agent action select the clicked project before opening the dialog, reusing the existing open-project path (App.tsx:121 already calls setSelectedProject) rather than a second ad-hoc setter. Then verify the dialog's three hooks all resolve to the clicked project.
queue.verify: A vitest test that asserts the POST URL carries the CLICKED project id when it differs from the selected one. Mutation-check it: revert the fix and watch that test fail by name before restoring.
queue.note: Consider whether threading an explicit projectId prop is ALSO worth doing as defence in depth. If it is cheap, do both; the operator's choice was about behaviour, not about forbidding belt-and-braces.
queue.outcome: Fixed in App.tsx: onAddAgent now navigates to the clicked project before opening the dialog, using the same projectDestination call onOpenProject already uses. New test src/__tests__/agentCreateProjectScope.test.tsx mounts App over a two-project rail; mutation-checked (revert -> exactly that test fails by name). tsc clean, vitest 1155 passed, eslint clean, bundle refreshed. Defence-in-depth prop threading deliberately NOT done - see the log entry for why.

queue.title: Open any AgentWeave project from any AgentWeave app — adopt an orphaned marker instead of refusing
queue.severity: high — this is the item the operator named as the point of the night
queue.system: openspec — this is a behaviour change to a specified capability, so it gets a proper change with a spec delta and a design rationale. The operator chose this explicitly over fixing it directly.
queue.evidence: hub/hub/project_lifecycle.py open_existing has three cases. Case 1 (existing_by_path, lines 67-75) opens. Case 2 (marker names a project THIS database has, lines 78-85) runs _guard_relocation and opens or correctly refuses a copy. Case 3 (marker names a project this database does NOT have, lines 86-90) refuses with 'marked directory is a copied or orphaned project identity'. Case 3 is the defect.
queue.why_adoption_is_safe: At case 3 the Hub knows two things: no project in this database is bound to this path (existing_by_path is None), and no project in this database holds the marker's id (marked_project is None). Nothing collides — the primary key and the path_key unique constraint are both free. Real copy detection lives in _guard_relocation (project_lifecycle.py:190-208), which fires on case 2 and refuses with 'project marker was copied while the registered directory is still available'. That guard is unchanged by this work and MUST stay green. The only scenario case 3 currently 'protects' against is a copy whose original lives in a database this Hub cannot see, has no authority over, and would collide with on worktrees and runs regardless of which id is used.
queue.also_fixes: Delete-then-re-add. ProjectLifecycleService.delete (project_lifecycle.py:156-167) is explicitly documented never to touch the filesystem (design D4), so the marker survives a delete naming an id the database just dropped. Re-adding the same folder hits case 3 and is refused. With adoption it works AND restores the same project id. Do not change D4 to fix this — adoption is the fix.
queue.do: Propose the change (/openspec-propose), write the spec delta against local-multi-project-workspace with the rejection reason for the current behaviour recorded, then implement: case 3 creates the project row with the MARKER'S id, seeds it as _seed_new_project does (runners + starter charters), records an adoption event, and opens.
queue.verify: New tests: (a) an orphaned marker is adopted and the project keeps its original id; (b) delete-then-reopen returns the same id; (c) two directories carrying the same marker — the second is still refused by _guard_relocation. Existing test_copied_marker_conflicts_until_explicitly_registered_as_new (hub/tests/test_project_lifecycle.py:75) must stay green untouched — it exercises case 2, not case 3, and is the proof the copy guard survived.
queue.note: Case 3 appears to have no test of its own today. Confirm that while implementing; if true, say so in the change's design as part of why the behaviour went unquestioned.
queue.outcome: Confirmed: case 3 had no test before this change. Proposed and validated openspec change at openspec/changes/portable-project-identity/ (capability is local-project-workspace, not local-multi-project-workspace as this item's title implied -- that capability name does not exist). Implemented in hub/hub/project_lifecycle.py open_existing: marked_project is None + not register_copy_as_new now constructs the Project row with the marker's own id, seeds it via the existing _seed_new_project, observes/writes-marker/commits, logs an adoption event, and returns -- instead of raising ProjectIdentityConflict. Two new mutation-checked tests in hub/tests/test_project_lifecycle.py (test_orphaned_marker_is_adopted_under_its_own_id, test_deleted_project_directory_is_adopted_back_under_the_same_id). All 19 tests in test_project_lifecycle.py + test_project_persistence.py pass; the existing case-2 copy-guard test is untouched and green. ruff and black clean. openspec validate --changes --strict passes. Not verified live in a browser (blocked by the no-Hub-restart limit, same as P1).

queue.title: Fix timestamps at the serialisation boundary
queue.evidence: Handoff 0060 recorded this as 'the better fix' and left it open. Confirmed live: hub/hub/db/models.py declares every timestamp column DateTime(timezone=True), but SQLite has no timezone storage, so a value written aware comes back naive once actually round-tripped through the DBAPI — three call sites (agent_status.py:22, api/v1/agents.py:528, scheduler.py:83) already carried a manual tzinfo-is-None workaround for their own in-process comparisons, independent confirmation the bug is real.
queue.do: Move the correction to where the Hub serialises the value rather than where the UI reads it, and retire whatever client-side compensation that makes redundant. Keep the exemptions that are genuinely client-side concerns.
queue.verify: Server-side tests on the serialised shape, plus the existing UI timestamp tests still green.
queue.outcome: Added hub.db.models.UTCDateTime, a TypeDecorator wrapping DateTime(timezone=True) that relabels a naive process_result_value as UTC once, at the ORM boundary. All 77 mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True)) declarations in models.py now use it, so every Pydantic response field and every raw .isoformat() call downstream (audited by grep across hub/hub) inherits the fix without individual changes — chosen over adding a UTCDateTime Pydantic field type to ~12 schema files because the TypeDecorator also covers the raw isoformat() call sites a schema-only fix could not reach. hub/ui/src/lib/hubTime.ts's hubDate() is now a thin new Date(value) pass-through (the ${value}Z-guessing hasTimezone() heuristic deleted); kept as a named function rather than inlined at its ~15 call sites because hubTime.test.ts's existing sweep test enforces exactly one seam. New hub/tests/test_timestamp_serialization.py (ORM round-trip through a second session, plus a GET against seeded runners) mutation-checked by reverting process_result_value to a no-op — both tests failed by name with the expected 'no UTC offset' message, then restored (note: git checkout -- on the first restore attempt wiped the whole file back to HEAD, not just the mutation; caught immediately via grep -c UTCDateTime and redone from the Edit calls). Measured: hub pytest full suite -n 4 — 2471 passed/75 skipped/1 xpassed in 174s (STATE.json's ~7min/600s-cap note was for the unparallelised run). vitest 1165/118 (-2, the two retired hubDate tests). tsc, eslint, ruff, black all clean. UI bundle rebuilt via scripts/refresh_ui_bundle.py and committed with its source. Not verified live in a browser — same no-restart limit as P1-P3. Open finding for a future iteration: no lint/test sweeps every DateTime(...) declaration in models.py the way hubTime.test.ts sweeps the client, so a future column bypassing UTCDateTime wouldn't be caught automatically.

queue.title: Close the D15 name-reuse hole
queue.evidence: A new agent taking an archived agent's name inherits the archived agent's creator privilege. Task A5.3 recorded this deliberately rather than fixing it.
queue.operator_decision: Strip the inherited privilege on reuse. Chosen over blocking reuse of archived names, because archiving and recreating under the same name is a thing the operator actually does and a permanent name reservation would be worse than the hole.
queue.do: A new agent taking a previously-archived name starts with no creator privilege over the old agent's artifacts. Names stay reusable.
queue.verify: A test that creates an agent, gives it a creator-privileged artifact, archives it, recreates the same name, and asserts the new agent cannot reach the old artifact.
queue.outcome: The literal scenario (archive + recreate the same name) does not reproduce today — reconfirmed independently, not just trusted from A5.3's 2026-08-19 note: `ix_agents_project_name` is an unconditional unique index on (project_id, name), and nothing renames an existing agent to free a name. The real, still-open gap A5.3 documented one layer down is what got closed: `_authorize_loop_task_creation` (hub/hub/api/v1/tasks.py) compared actor.agent to AIJob.agent as bare strings, never consulting the agents table, so a Run minted under an archived name kept that name's loop-creator authority. Fixed in two parts: (1) hub/hub/api/v1/agent_trigger.py's trigger_agent_directly (used by turn_scheduler and scheduler._do_fire_job) and the POST /agent/trigger route both now refuse with 409 if Agent.lifecycle == 'archived', closing 'nothing runs an archived agent' everywhere at once, not just the loop-authority angle; (2) _authorize_loop_task_creation now looks up the Agent row behind job.agent and refuses if it exists and reads archived — deliberately NOT refused when no Agent row exists at all, since that shape is the existing contract every _active_run-style test fixture in this codebase relies on (first version without that carve-out broke 4 unrelated tests, caught by insisting on the full suite rather than trusting the targeted files). The pre-existing D15 test in hub/tests/test_tasks.py was flipped per its own docstring's instruction, renamed to test_d15_an_archived_creators_run_no_longer_controls_its_loop, now asserting 403 — its old fixture had a latent bug (set archived_at but never lifecycle, so it was never actually archived by the model's own definition), fixed in the rewrite. New test_trigger_refuses_an_archived_agent added to test_agent_trigger.py. Both fixes mutation-checked (revert -> exact test fails by name -> restore). Full suite `pytest tests/ -n 4`: 2472 passed / 75 skipped / 1 xpassed (2471 before, +1 net — the D15 test was rewritten in place, not added). ruff, black clean; mypy zero errors attributable to either touched file. hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py's _require_agent_job_allowance, the other function A5.3 named, was deliberately left untouched — it gates the CURRENT caller's own live run against a project-wide allowance, not a stored creator identity, so its exposure to an archived name closes as a side effect of fix (1) rather than needing its own change. No UI touched, no bundle rebuild. Not verified live in a browser, but this iteration is backend-only so the no-Hub-restart limit that blocked P1-P4's live checks doesn't apply — there is no UI surface to check.
